name: North Ridge
approach: Same Thunder Creek Trailhead approach as the East Slope route (Colonial Creek Campground on SR 20, past McAllister and Tricouni Camps, up 'Lucky Ridge' to a bivy at ~6,000 ft near the toe of the Borealis Glacier) — the North Ridge is reached by traversing around the lake instead of climbing the glacier from camp.

approach_variants.name: Round to the unnamed glacier north of the peak
approach_variants.notes:
This is a genuinely obscure line and every recorded approach to it is a variation on getting round to the mountain's north side, which no other Primus route visits.

The first recorded ascent reached it from the Klawatti side: descend a couloir where the North Klawatti Glacier meets Primus's west ridge, then traverse an unnamed glacier north of Primus to the foot of the crest. The first-ascent account says in as many words that it was unlikely this approach had been used before.

Other parties have come from the Thunder Creek side instead — the same trailhead, ford and Lucky Ridge climb as the East Slope, to a bivy near 6,000 ft at the toe of the Borealis Glacier — and then reached the ridge by circling the glacial lake at the glacier's terminus and crossing a short section of glacier to the base, rather than climbing the glacier toward Lucky Pass. One party took that line specifically because conditions at the standard Primus-Tricouni saddle were hazardous that day.

The ridge itself is about 1,000 ft and took the first-ascent party roughly an hour.
approach_variants.season: Mid-July through August; a documented late-September attempt found the crux notch glazed with bullet ice and the loose rock unbonded, which made the route markedly harder and more dangerous
hazards: Very loose, serrated rock along the entire crest — blocks and towers described as good but somewhat loose
A 5.6 crux notch with no fixed protection: natural gear and slung blocks only
Verglas glazing the notch in cool or wet weather, which is what defeated a late-September attempt
Committing retreat once above the crux — the recommended descent is the East Ridge to Lucky Pass, not this ridge
Glacier travel on an unnamed, rarely visited glacier with no established line
approach_variants.baseFinding:
The test is which side of the mountain you are on, and it is decided by whether you had to go down to get there. Every approach to this ridge involves losing height onto a glacier north of Primus — down a couloir from the North Klawatti Glacier where it meets Primus's west ridge, or down and around the glacial lake at the Borealis Glacier's terminus. If your day has been a continuous climb, you have not reached this route.

The negative test is unambiguous and it is the one to carry: Lucky Pass is not this route. If you are standing at a col at about 7,200 ft at the head of the Borealis Glacier, with Tricouni Peak's route splitting off east, you are at the start of the East Slope — a class 3 walk. The North Ridge is reached by turning away from that pass, not through it.

What the base itself looks like: the foot of a 1,000 ft crest of blocks and towers, met from a glacier rather than from a notch. There is no published cairn, marker or fixed anchor at the start; the ridge is very rarely repeated and nothing on it should be assumed to be in place.

Confirm on the ground you climb, not on the approach: the lower ridge is 3rd and 4th class blocks and towers; the upper ridge is banded rock at low fifth, and that banding is what the first-ascent party singled out. A ridge that stays third class to the summit is not this one — and a ridge that never carried you above a glacier on the peak's north side never was.

waypoints.name: Thunder Creek Trailhead
waypoints.note: South end of Colonial Creek Campground on Hwy 20.
waypoints.directions: Drive SR 20 east past Newhalem and Diablo to Colonial Creek Campground on Diablo Lake's Thunder Arm, just past milepost 130, and turn into the south loop. Park in the lot above the boat ramp; the Thunder Creek Trail starts at the south end of the campground near the amphitheater, at about 1,200 ft. Overnight stays need a North Cascades wilderness permit.

waypoints.name: Primus Peak
waypoints.note: Via McAllister Camp (~6 mi in) and Lucky Ridge to the bivy at the toe of the Borealis Glacier, then around the glacial lake and across a short stretch of glacier to the foot of the North Ridge. The usual descent is the East Ridge to Lucky Pass (7,200 ft) and down the Borealis Glacier.

_raw.approach: Thunder Creek Trailhead near Colonial Creek Campground
_raw.pickup_deadline: Permits must be picked up by 11am on trip start date
_raw.special_hazards: Exposed climbing and glacier travel required; exposed sections on route
_raw.seasonal_availability: 60% reserved online during peak season (approx May-Sept); 40% first-come-first-served

access.fees: $10 per person plus a $6 non-refundable reservation fee for an overnight backcountry permit; youth 15 and under free. The fee season runs mid-May to early October.
access.rules: Group size capped at 6 in off-trail cross-country zones (12 in on-trail corridors). Boston Basin camping restricted to two designated sites (Low Camp ~5,300 ft, High Camp ~6,400 ft). Bear canisters required in some zones — free loaners at permit offices.
access.closures: Thunder Creek Fire: North Cascades National Park's fire-closure list (updated September 14, 2026; no end date given) closes the Thunder Creek Trail from the Fisher Creek Trail junction to Park Creek Pass for the Thunder Creek Fire, along with Junction Camp, Skagit Queen Camp and Thunder Basin Camp (hiker and stock sites), and prohibits cross-country travel from the closed trail. This route leaves the Thunder Creek Trail at Tricouni Camp, below the Fisher Creek junction, so its approach is outside the closed section. North Cascades National Park: (360) 854-7200.
access.land_manager: National Park Service — North Cascades National Park (Stephen Mather Wilderness)

overnight_permit.what: North Cascades NP wilderness permit — limited, with a fee
overnight_permit.where: Reserve on Recreation.gov, or get a walk-up permit in person at the Marblemount Wilderness Information Center up to a day ahead. Camps above Thunder Creek fall in cross-country zones.
